title: Interim Deployment status automatically imposes a 100% Capital Ratio Requirement instead of a venue-specific risk assessment
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.1.2.5.1 states that the JTRSY Instance "is currently defined as an **Interim Deployment** (see A.1.10.2.3.2.2.2) and **as such** has CRR of 100%." A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.2.2.5.1 says the same for BUIDL.

The words "as such" carry the mechanism. The Capital Ratio Requirement is not derived from an assessment of Anemoy, Securitize, or the underlying treasury exposure — it follows automatically from the deployment's *lifecycle stage*. A 100% CRR means the position must be fully backed by capital, so it consumes no leverage and generates no net balance-sheet exposure for Sky.

This solves a real bootstrapping problem. A risk framework cannot price a venue it has not observed, and observation requires deploying into it. Rather than guessing a CRR from an incomplete assessment, the framework applies the maximally conservative value by default and lets the deployment produce the evidence that justifies relaxing it.

The cost is precise: an Interim Deployment is capital-inefficient by construction, so a venue's yield can never justify itself during the testing period — every Interim Deployment looks unattractive on a return-on-capital basis while it is being evaluated. That makes the *duration* of interim status the important variable, and it also explains why these Instances pair the 100% CRR with a small Maximum Allocation: the framework is buying information, and it has priced the purchase rather than the position.

This is a reusable pattern for admitting unknown counterparties: make the trial risk-free to the balance sheet and cap its size, rather than attempting to assess what cannot yet be assessed.
